{{short description|Extinct language of eastern Brazil}} {{Infobox language | name = Pankararú | states = [[Brazil]] | region = [[Pernambuco]], [[Alagoas]] | extinct = by 1961 | familycolor = American | family = [[Language isolate]] | lc1 = pax | ld1 = Pankararé | lc2 = | ld2 = | glotto = pank1250 | glottoname = Pankararu | glotto2 = pank1235 | glottoname2 = Pankarare | ethnicity = 8.184 {{ill|Pankararú people|lt=Pankararú|pt|Pancararus}} (2014),{{Cite web |title=Pankararu - Indigenous Peoples in Brazil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/en/Povo:Pankararu |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}} ?1,648 Pankararé (2014){{Cite web |title=Pankararé - Povos Indígenas no Brasil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Pankarar%C3%A9 |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}} | dia1 = Pankararú | dia2 = ?Pankararé | map = Atikum_e_Pankará.png | mapcaption = Map of Atikum and Pankará peoples and languages | altname = Brancararu | iso3 = paz | iso3comment = (Pankararú) }} '''Pankararú''' (''Pancaré, Pankaré, Pancaru, Pankaruru, Pankarará, Pankaravu, Pankaroru, Pankarú, Brancararu'') is an [[extinct language]], probably a language isolate, of eastern Brazil. There are 6,000 [[Pankararú people|ethnic Pankararú]], but they all speak Portuguese. In 1961, only two elders could remember anything of the language. Today, they live in Brejo dos Padres and other villages of [[Tacaratu]], [[Pernambuco]] State. The language was originally spoken between the [[Moxotó River]] and the [[Pajeú River]].{{cite book |last=Loukotka |first=Čestmír |author-link=Čestmír Loukotka |title=Classification of South American Indian languages |url=https://archive.org/details/classificationof0007louk |url-access=registration |publisher=UCLA Latin American Center |year=1968 |location=Los Angeles}} In the 19th century the people split into multiple ethnic groups, including the Pankararú and the Pankararé. One quarter of the Pankararé retain their traditional religion. Their language, however, is unattested,{{cite web| editor-last1= Hammarström| editor-first1 = Harald| editor-last2 = Forke| editor-first2 = Robert| editor-last3 = Haspelmath| editor-first3 = Martin| editor-last4 = Bank| editor-first4 = Sebastian| year = 2020|title = Pankararé | work = [[Glottolog]] 4.3| url = https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/pank1235}} and can only be assumed to be a dialect of Pankararu. == Classification == Pankararú has no proven relatives and remains unclassified. Meader (1978) found that of 80 known lexical items, 26 are clearly cognate with Tupian languages. He speculates that the last speakers of Pankararú may therefore have been bilingual in Tupi. The identity of the rest of the vocabulary has not been identified, and Pankararú may be a [[language isolate]]. Loukotka (1968) also lists these languages as being formerly spoken in [[Tacaratu]], [[Pernambuco]] State. It is not known whether or not they were related to Pankararú: *''Jeriticó'' or ''Jiripancó''{{Cite web |title=Jiripancó - Povos Indígenas no Brasil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Jiripanc%C3%B3 |access-date=2025-09-25 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}} – village of Pindaé near Brejo dos Padres in Tacaratu, Pernambuco. Survivors now speak only Portuguese. *''Macarú'' – village of Brejo dos Padres, Tacaratu. A few survivors now speak only Portuguese. The original languages of the ''Koiupanká''{{Cite web |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Koiupank%C3%A1 |title=Koiupanká |website=Povos Indígenas no Brasil |language=pt |access-date=29 January 2020}} and ''Karuazu''{{Cite web |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Karuazu |title=Karuazu |website=Povos Indígenas no Brasil |language=pt |access-date=29 January 2020}} may have been related or identical to Pankararú. ''Kalankó'' (''Cacalancó''), with descendants now living in [[Água Branca, Alagoas]], may have also been related to, or identical with, Pankararú.{{Cite web |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Kalank%C3%B3 |title=Kalankó |website=Povos Indígenas no Brasil |language=pt |access-date=29 January 2020}} ==Vocabulary== ===Pompeu (1958)=== Language variety from Pompeu (1958), originally collected by Carlos Estêvam:{{Cite journal |last=Pompeu Sobrinho |first=Thomaz |date=1958 |title=Línguas Tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: Alguns vocabulários inéditos |url=https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/biblio%3Apompeu-1958-desconhecidas/Pompeu_1958_LinguasTapuiasDesconhecidasNE_BA2n1.pdf |journal=Boletim de Antropologia (Fortaleza-Ceará) |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=3–19}} :{| class="wikitable sortable" !
